one_liner: Young pure-Rust JavaScript engine (register VM). Its own V8-suite table puts it 2.4% behind QuickJS overall, and its RegExp lead is a bug.
what_it_does: Pipa is a JavaScript interpreter written in Rust and published as the pipa-js crate (library name pipa) plus a pipa command-line binary. Hosts create a JSRuntime and a JSContext, call eval or eval_async, and register Rust functions with register_global_builtin. Scripts can be precompiled to .jsc bytecode at -O0 to -O3. It is not a drop-in for QuickJS's C API, and despite the 'ES2023 compliant' label its own test262 table shows Proxy at 0%, Promise 5.6%, Set 18.8%, Map 22.2% and RegExp 42.3%.
how_it_is_fast: Values are NaN-boxed 64-bit words (tag in bits 47-50, pointers compressed by a 3-bit shift). Code compiles to register-based bytecode with a peephole pass, and the VM keeps shapes and inline caches for property access. The heap uses a nursery plus a tri-colour mark collector (32 MB minimum threshold), and regex literals are compiled once per site (regex_lit_cache). The regex engine dispatches to a literal or class DFA, a few hard-coded class matchers (\d+, \w+, 'foo|bar') or a backtracking NFA. The large RegExp-suite lead does not come from these: see gotchas.
when_to_use: Experiments where a Rust host wants an embedded JavaScript engine with no C toolchain (build with default-features = false), running simple ASCII, numeric or object-heavy scripts.
Numeric array code: NavierStokes scored 2087 against qjs's 1759 (+18.6%), the only suite where pipa's lead is not explained by a bug.
Workloads like Richards, DeltaBlue, Crypto and Splay, where pipa came within 2-10% of qjs while staying in pure Rust.
As a faster pure-Rust option than Boa: the same table has pipa at 1075 against Boa's 185 (about 5.8x, derived from page data), if you can accept far lower conformance.
when_not_to_use: Any script that relies on regular expressions: String.prototype.replace and match with a RegExp argument search for the pattern's source text literally, and RegExp.prototype.exec returns no capture groups.
When speed is the goal: QuickJS scores higher overall in pipa's own table (1101 vs 1075) and is much faster on RayTrace (-53.5%) and EarleyBoyer (-33.1%).
Async or meta-programming code: Promise passes 5.6% of test262, Proxy 0%, Map 22.2% and Set 18.8%.
Non-ASCII text: strings are UTF-8 indexed by code point, so length, charAt and indices differ from JavaScript's UTF-16 rules, and indexing is O(n) on non-ASCII strings.
Production systems: first commit 2026-05-20, version 0.1.8, 274 crates.io downloads, no commits since 2026-07-04.

integration.form: crate (pipa-js on crates.io, library name pipa) plus the pipa CLI binary
integration.dependencies: none with default-features = false; the default repl feature pulls in fetch and process: rustls (ring backend), webpki-roots, flate2, libc and rustyline
integration.min_toolchain: Rust edition 2024 (so Rust 1.85 or newer); no rust-version declared
integration.platforms: not documented; pure Rust, but the NaN-boxing assumes 64-bit targets with 8-byte-aligned heap pointers below 2^50
integration.thread_safety: not documented; values hold raw pointers into the context's heap, so use one runtime and context per thread. set_interrupt(&JSRuntime, bool) sets an atomic flag to stop a running script.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — it runs the same JavaScript source, but the embedding API is pipa's own Rust API (not QuickJS's C API), and core built-ins (RegExp, Promise, Proxy, Map/Set) do not follow the spec

gotchas: The RegExp score (841 vs qjs 306, +174.8%) comes from a correctness bug. In src/builtins/string.rs, string_replace with a RegExp argument takes the regex source string and runs s.find(&pattern), a literal substring search, instead of the regex engine. This branch is identical at commit 4a4dfd0 (2026-06-14, the last change before the 2026-06-15 table) and at HEAD (0.1.8). In the V8 RegExp suite, 712 .replace calls all take a regex (690 replace with ''), so most never run a regex. regexp_exec (466 exec calls) returns only match[0] with length 1, without capture groups. The suite discards every result, so nothing catches this. Without RegExp, pipa's geometric mean is 1114 vs qjs 1321, about 16% slower (derived from page data).

String.prototype.match with a RegExp also does a literal search of the pattern source. From reading src/regexp/fast_engine.rs (not run): the literal-DFA and class fast paths are picked from the pattern text alone without the flags, so a literal pattern with the i flag appears to match case-sensitively.

Strings are interned UTF-8 atoms (every new string goes through a hash-map intern) indexed by code point. length counts code points, not UTF-16 units, so non-BMP characters differ from other engines. regexp_exec slices the input at lastIndex as a UTF-8 byte offset, so a lastIndex set inside a multi-byte character will panic (from reading). The CLI's release profile uses panic = abort.

Harness: bench-v8.sh runs each engine as one process on boa-dev's combined.js (each suite runs at least 1 s and 32 iterations; the total is the geometric mean). It uses whatever qjs is on PATH (version unknown), names no CPU, and reports status 'ok' whenever a SCORE line appears, even if the process exited with errors. A failing suite would silently drop out of the geometric mean. The repo has no LICENSE file; MIT is stated only in Cargo.toml and the README, and the README's dependency snippets still name 0.1.1 and 0.1.2.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Rarely: QuickJS (and its forks gkurt/quickjs and PrimJS) is faster overall in pipa's own table and far more complete, so it is the default. Pick pipa only to prototype a pure-Rust, no-C JavaScript embedding, and avoid regex-dependent code. Roto is the faster Rust-hosted choice if you do not need JavaScript itself.
verified_claims_summary: The README table (2026-06-15, matching the pipa-js 0.1.7 release date) is one run per engine of the V8 benchmark suite (combined.js from boa-dev/data) via bench-v8.sh, with pipa built using cargo --release (opt-level 3, LTO, codegen-units 1, panic abort). qjs came from PATH with no version stated, and no CPU or rustc version is given. Pipa's total of 1075 is 2.4% below qjs's 1101 (I recomputed both geometric means from the per-suite rows). Its only wins are RegExp, which is invalid because replace and match do not run the regex engine, and NavierStokes (+18.6%). The README headline 'outperforms QuickJS' is not supported.
status_note: Pre-1.0 and quiet since 2026-07-04 (240 commits since 2026-05-20, 62 stars, 274 crates.io downloads). It has a RegExp correctness bug behind its headline benchmark win and low test262 coverage, and its MIT licence is declared only in Cargo.toml and the README. Treat it as an experiment, not a QuickJS replacement.
